strings.name: Ayanna Howard
strings.summary: Ayanna Howard researches robotics, AI and assistive technology. She worked at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory and Georgia Tech and founded Zyrobotics to translate research into technology for children with diverse learning needs. In 2021 she became Ohio State’s first woman engineering dean; in 2026 she became Spelman College’s 12th president. Research and products reflect team contributions; research descriptions do not establish clinical effectiveness.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Post-appointment reporting confirms her 2026 role. Sources differ on her early JPL start date; the entire period is not described as full-time employment.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced robotics, assistive technology and AI research, focusing on applications in children’s rehabilitation and inclusive technology.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from Brown in 1993; earned a USC PhD in electrical engineering in 1999.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research areas
strings.facts.f2.value: Human–robot interaction, autonomous systems and assistive technology for children with diverse learning needs.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Human-centered robotics
strings.highlights.h1.text: Combines sensing, learning and autonomous control to explore cooperation between people and robots.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research translation and educational leadership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Advanced assistive learning technology through Zyrobotics and educational access through university leadership.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Becomes Spelman College president
strings.timeline.t1.text: Becomes its 12th president. The June announcement supplies the effective date; WABE’s August 21 interview report confirms she has taken office.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Submits congressional AI testimony
strings.timeline.t2.text: Addresses the U.S. Joint Economic Committee on AI, the economy, governance and workforce development.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes Ohio State engineering dean
strings.timeline.t3.text: Begins her term as the college’s first woman dean.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leads the School of Interactive Computing
strings.timeline.t4.text: Becomes the school’s chair at Georgia Tech; the appointment was announced in December 2017.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Founds Zyrobotics
strings.timeline.t5.text: Translates research into assistive learning and educational products for children with diverse learning needs.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins Georgia Tech
strings.timeline.t6.text: Leaves JPL, joins the university and establishes the HumAnS lab; the month comes from her IEEE oral history.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns an electrical engineering PhD
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completes doctoral research at USC, including robotic hands capable of changing shape and grasping objects.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates from Brown
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earns an undergraduate engineering degree, then continues her studies at USC.
